title: Role resolver and guardrails for multi-tenant resource hierarchy
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Design and implement the Role Resolver component for RBAC v2 that deterministically evaluates roles and permissions across a multi-tenant resource hierarchy. This ticket covers the resolution algorithm, how role bindings are sourced (SSO/SAML, SCIM, console-assigned, tenancy inheritance), audit logging hooks for every decision, and the guardrails required for admin features (delegated admin, emergency break-glass, and role review). The outcome is a reference implementation + API contract and a migration plan from RBAC v1 to v2 with shadow-mode testing.
acceptance_criteria: Role Resolver returns a reproducible list of effective grants for a (principal, resource, action) query within 10ms p50 in our test harness
Decision logs emitted for every authorization query contain required fields: decision_id, principal_id, role_sources, evaluated_scopes, policy_version, cache_status
SAML attribute-to-role mapping and SCIM group sync implemented and tested end-to-end in staging
Delegated admin flows enforce locality and time-bounded elevation; break-glass issues create an auditable one-time token
Migration can be run in shadow mode for a production tenant for 14 days with telemetry comparing v1 and v2 results
Feature flags and rollout plan exist to enable gradual opt-in per-tenant and per-route
design_decisions: Resolution precedence: explicit resource-level binding > resource-ancestor bindings (nearest ancestor wins in conflicts) > tenant-level bindings > global bindings
Role composition: roles are additive by default; explicit deny not supported in initial v2 release (denies planned for v2.1 after usage analysis)
Role source canonicalization: annotate each binding with source_type (sso, scim, console, api), source_id, and source_timestamp
Caching: cache effective grants keyed by (principal_id, resource_id, token_version) with TTL tuned to 30s and explicit invalidation on role changes
API contract: /auth/evaluate returns flat array of grants and a decision_id; /audit/decisions stores full evaluation payload
Back-compat: provide compatibility layer that accepts v1 policy shape and translates to v2 internal structures for the transition period
migration_plan: Phase 0 - Audit only: enable shadow-mode that evaluates v2 decisions but does not affect enforcement; collect divergence metrics for 14 days
Phase 1 - Opt-in tenants: expose console toggle + API header to opt-in tenants; provide migration helper to convert role bindings
Phase 2 - Default opt-out with enforcement exceptions: enable v2 enforcement for new tenants; existing tenants continue v1 unless they opt-in
Phase 3 - Removal: after 90 days of opt-in campaign and no significant regressions, plan deprecation timeline for v1
Migration artifacts: migration scripts, compatibility middleware, and reconciliation tooling to align group mappings (SCIM)
tasks: Spec: write decision log schema and example payloads (Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RBAC/Decision+Log+Schema)
Implement role-resolver core algorithm in auth-service (repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/auth-service)
Integrate SAML attribute mapping + SCIM group sync codepath and unit tests
Console: add tenant-level RBAC v2 toggle and role binding viewer
Telemetry: add divergence metric dashboard (Grafana) and SLI for evaluation latency
Create migration playbook and runbook for customer-facing SREs
Security review and threat-model session scheduled
risks: Divergent semantics between v1 and v2 causing unexpected permission changes for customers
Performance impact on tail latency due to deeper ancestor scans; mitigated by caching and ancestor precomputation
SAML attribute inconsistencies across IdPs leading to incorrect mappings; mitigated by preflight SCIM sync and mapping guides
Incomplete audit logs (missing context) could impede investigations; decision log schema must be comprehensive
Emergency elevation misuse if break-glass tokens are not time-bound or lack manual approval steps
